related_questions.question: What's the most accurate test for COVID?

text_blocks.snippet: The most accurate COVID-19 test depends on the context, but generally, PCR tests performed in a lab are considered the gold standard for detecting active infections. Rapid antigen tests, including those available for at-home use, are more convenient but less sensitive, particularly during early or asymptomatic infection.

list.title: PCR tests:
list.snippet: These tests are highly sensitive and can detect even tiny amounts of viral genetic material. They are the most accurate for diagnosing COVID-19, but they require specialized equipment and lab processing, making them less convenient for widespread use.

list.title: Rapid antigen tests:
list.snippet: These tests detect specific proteins (antigens) on the virus. They are faster and easier to use, making them suitable for rapid screening. However, they are less sensitive than PCR tests, particularly during early infection or in asymptomatic individuals.

list.title: At-home rapid antigen tests:
list.snippet: These tests are convenient for quick screening but may have a higher chance of false negatives (especially with newer variants).

list.title: When to use which test:
list.snippet: For the most accurate results, especially if you have symptoms or have been exposed, PCR tests performed in a lab are recommended. If you need a quick result for travel or other purposes, at-home rapid antigen tests are an option, but it's important to be aware of their limitations.
